description: Is the branch-point count 6 of the chi(A) = -6 chain FORCED or merely IN RANGE? Exact-rational genericity probe over five candidate sources, including the finite-subgroup/ADE route. Companion to the sorry-free Lean QOU/BringsSurface/BranchPointSixNotForced.lean.
name: chi-branch-point-count-genericity
tier: exact structural probe (no fit, nothing wired; scope-(a)/(b) framing per AGENTS.md)
arithmetic: exact int / fractions.Fraction throughout; no float64

checks.name: T1_minus_six_not_singled_out
checks.detail: -4, -6 and -8 are all admissible; Step 5 alone picks -6 out of a countably infinite set

checks.name: T2_six_points_degree_four_spans_genus_0_to_6
checks.detail: R in [6, 18] gives genus [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6] -- the branch COUNT alone determines nothing near g = 4

checks.name: T2_corpus_R_is_what_gives_minus_six
checks.detail: chi = -6 needs R = 14 at d = 4 and R = 12 at d = 3; both corpus blocks are consistent only as different maps

checks.name: T3_weierstrass_count_is_sixty
checks.detail: g^3 - g at g = 4 is 60, and Aut(B) = S_5 acts TRANSITIVELY on all of them -- so there is no set of six for an S_3 to act on

checks.name: T3_sixty_splits_as_six_by_ten
checks.detail: 60 = 6 x 10: six Weierstrass points fixed by each of the ten TRANSPOSITIONS in S_5 (same source, next paragraph) -- the real carrier of the 6 is an involution, not an S_3

checks.name: T3_transposition_quotient_gives_minus_six
checks.detail: chi(B) = 2*chi(torus) - 6 = -6, so B/<tau> has genus 1 -- a coherent reading of Step 5, but still read off Bring

checks.name: T3_ramification_six_not_forced_by_chi
checks.detail: (d,h,R) = (2,1,6), (2,2,2) and (3,2,0) all give -6: the 6 arrives with the choice of base genus, not from chi

checks.name: T4_pair_brackets_every_genus
checks.detail: T_(2,2g+1)/T_(2,2g+3) brackets every g in 1..12; at g = 4 that pair is (9, 11) -- exactly the corpus's (9, 11). The constraints restate the target rather than derive it

checks.name: T5_klein_relation_holds_for_every_family
checks.detail: chi_orb = 2 - sum_i (1 - 1/m_i) = 2/|G| exactly for all 13 families -- cross-checks every cone order and orbit size

checks.name: T5_six_is_NOT_an_icosahedral_orbit_size
checks.detail: icosahedral orbits are [30, 20, 12] -- all >= 12, so no orbit reading of 'branch points on P(V)' can return 6 for E_8

checks.name: T5_six_IS_a_tetrahedral_and_octahedral_orbit_size
checks.detail: tetrahedral [6, 4, 4], octahedral [12, 8, 6] -- an orbit reading of 6 points AWAY from the icosahedral case

checks.name: T5_sylow_arithmetic_leaves_two_candidates
checks.detail: n_5(A_5) in [1, 6], n_3(A_4) in [1, 4], n_3(S_4) in [1, 4]; simplicity of A_5 picks 6 -- that last input is cited, not derived

checks.name: T5_sylow_and_orbit_readings_disagree
checks.detail: on the icosahedral group the Sylow reading gives 6 and the orbit reading does not; on the tetrahedral group the orbit reading gives 6 and the Sylow reading does not. 6 is a property of the CHOSEN INVARIANT, not of the ADE type

checks.name: T5_six_occurs_once_among_A5_invariants
checks.detail: of 16 natural integer invariants of A_5, exactly 1 equals 6, and it is n_5. So 6 is not generic for A_5 -- but it is also not selected by anything in the axioms

checks.name: T6_transitivity_narrows_chi_to_two_values
checks.detail: homogeneity narrows chi(A) from the infinite set of T1 to [-4, -6]

checks.name: T6_order_five_selects_bring
checks.detail: by Cauchy an order-5 automorphism exists iff 5 | |Aut|: {'bring_g4': 120, 'klein_g3': 168, 's4_curve_g3': 24} -- only the genus-4 case qualifies

verdict.ade_route_scope: scope-(b) for the SPECIFIC implication 'icosahedral type => six branch points on P(V)': the invariant is the orbit-size formula |G|/m_i and it is proved, and the icosahedral orbits are 30/20/12. NOT a claim that no finite-group route can produce a 6 -- three other ADE types do.
verdict.finiteness_gap: su2_emergence_rank_forced constrains G only by 'unitary and det 1', which SU(2) itself satisfies. The ADE list classifies FINITE subgroups, so it does not apply to the object the axioms deliver. This is prior to the type question.
verdict.sharpest_open_statement: Steps 3+4 pin chi(A) to the non-positive even integers and no further; every candidate source tested here either restates the target (torus-knot brackets, T4), reads it off Bring (Weierstrass / transposition fixed points, T3), or fails to produce a 6 at all (ADE orbits, T5). The one hypothesis that narrows without naming 6 is transitivity of Aut on the Weierstrass points, which gives chi in {-4, -6} (T6); separating those two needs an order-5 automorphism. Both are group-theoretic and neither is derived from the five QOU axioms.

q0AnchorReason: q0-free: the probe is exact integer / Fraction combinatorics (Euler characteristics, Riemann-Hurwitz, finite-rotation-group orbit and Sylow counts). No substrate parameter is read anywhere in the import cone, so neither the ideal-muon nor the physical-proton layer applies.
